subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Determination of Functional Currency - Primary vs Secondary Factors
question: Global Exports Ltd. is incorporated in India. 85% of its sales revenues are invoiced and collected in US Dollars (USD). Labor, materials, and local compliance costs are incurred and settled in Indian Rupees (INR). Financing was raised in USD bonds on the Singapore exchange. Under Ind AS 21, what are the primary factors in determining the functional currency?
options: The currency of the country in which the registered corporate office is situated (INR).

The currency that mainly influences sales prices for goods and services, and the currency of the country whose competitive forces and regulations mainly determine the sales prices, along with the currency that mainly influences labor, material, and other operating costs.
The currency chosen by the Board of Directors.
The presentation currency of the parent company.
ref: Ind AS 21 (The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates) - Paragraphs 9-10: Primary Factors for Functional Currency
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 9 states that the primary factors are: (a) the currency that mainly influences sales prices for goods and services; and (b) the currency of the country whose competitive forces and regulations determine sales prices; and (c) the currency that mainly influences labor, material and other costs of providing goods or services. Secondary factors include financing and operating cash flow retention.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Monetary vs Non-Monetary Items at Reporting Date
question: On 31st March 2024, an Indian entity (functional currency INR) holds the following foreign currency items denominated in USD: (i) Trade Receivables of $100,000; (ii) Foreign equity investment at FVOCI of $50,000; (iii) Inventory acquired for $40,000 carried at cost; and (iv) Trade Payables of $80,000. Which of these are 'monetary items' to be translated at the closing spot exchange rate under Ind AS 21?
options: All four items.

Trade Receivables ($100,000) and Trade Payables ($80,000) are monetary items translated at the closing rate with exchange differences to P&L; Inventory (cost) and Equity at FVOCI are non-monetary items.
Only the equity investment.
Only Trade Receivables.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraphs 16 & 23: Monetary vs Non-Monetary Items
explanation: Ind AS 21 defines monetary items as units of currency held and assets and liabilities to be received or paid in a fixed or determinable number of units of currency (e.g. receivables, cash, payables). Non-monetary items have the absence of a right to receive or deliver a fixed number of units of currency (inventory, PPE, equity investments). Monetary items are translated at the closing rate with exchange differences recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Non-Monetary Item Carried at Fair Value
question: An entity holds an investment property in London denominated in British Pounds (GBP). It measures the property at Fair Value under Ind AS 40 / Ind AS 113. On 31st March 2024, the fair value is determined in GBP. At what exchange rate should the property be translated into INR, and where is the resulting foreign exchange difference recognized?
options: Historical exchange rate at the date of original acquisition; gain to P&L.

Exchange rate at the date when the fair value was determined (closing rate); the exchange difference is recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss (in the same manner as the fair value gain or loss under Ind AS 40).
Average exchange rate for the year; difference to OCI.
Historical cost rate without any translation.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraphs 23(c) & 30: Non-Monetary Items Measured at Fair Value
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 23(c) states that non-monetary items that are measured at fair value in a foreign currency shall be translated using the exchange rates at the date when the fair value was measured. Under Paragraph 30, when a gain or loss on a non-monetary item is recognized in profit or loss, any exchange component of that gain or loss shall be recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Translation of Foreign Operation to Presentation Currency
question: Indian Parent Ltd. (INR presentation currency) consolidates its 100% US subsidiary (USD functional currency). In translating the US subsidiary's balance sheet and P&L into INR under Ind AS 21, what exchange rates must be applied?
options: All assets, liabilities, income, and expenses are translated at the closing exchange rate.

Assets and liabilities (both monetary and non-monetary) are translated at the closing rate at the date of that balance sheet; income and expenses are translated at exchange rates at the dates of the transactions (or an appropriate average rate); all resulting exchange differences are recognized in Other Comprehensive Income (Foreign Currency Translation Reserve - FCTR).
All items translated at historical rates.
Assets at historical rate, liabilities at closing rate.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraphs 39-40: Translation to Presentation Currency
explanation: Under Ind AS 21 Paragraph 39: (a) assets and liabilities for each balance sheet presented shall be translated at the closing rate at the date of that balance sheet; (b) income and expenses for each statement of profit and loss shall be translated at exchange rates at the dates of the transactions (average rate); and (c) all resulting exchange differences shall be recognized in Other Comprehensive Income (accumulated in FCTR).

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Recycling of Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR)
question: Indian Parent Ltd. sells its entire 100% equity stake in its US subsidiary. Over the 5-year holding period, cumulative foreign currency translation gains of ₹50 Crores had been recognized in OCI and accumulated in FCTR. How is the accumulated FCTR treated upon full disposal of the foreign operation under Ind AS 21?
options: Retained permanently in equity without reclassification.

Reclassified ('recycled') in full from Other Comprehensive Income (FCTR) to the Statement of Profit and Loss as a reclassification adjustment within the total gain or loss on disposal of the foreign operation.
Transferred directly to Securities Premium.
Written off against goodwill.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 48: Disposal of a Foreign Operation and Recycling of FCTR
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 48 states: 'On the disposal of a foreign operation, the cumulative amount of the exchange differences relating to that foreign operation, recognized in other comprehensive income and accumulated in the separate component of equity, shall be reclassified from equity to profit or loss (as a reclassification adjustment) when the gain or loss on disposal is recognized.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Net Investment in a Foreign Operation
question: Indian Parent Ltd. extends an interest-free loan of $10,000,000 to its wholly-owned UK subsidiary. The loan agreement specifies that repayment is neither planned nor likely to occur in the foreseeable future. In substance, the loan forms part of Parent Ltd.'s net investment in the UK subsidiary. In the consolidated financial statements of the group, where are the foreign exchange differences on this loan recognized under Ind AS 21?
options: Recognized in the Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss.
Recognized in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) and accumulated in the Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR), to be reclassified to profit or loss on disposal of the net investment.
Recognized as an addition to share capital.
Eliminated against inter-company revenue.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraphs 15 & 32: Monetary Item Forming Part of Net Investment
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 15 defines an item for which settlement is neither planned nor likely to occur in the foreseeable future as, in substance, part of the entity's net investment in that foreign operation. Under Paragraph 32, exchange differences arising on such monetary items in consolidated financial statements shall be recognized initially in Other Comprehensive Income and reclassified to profit or loss on disposal.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 29: Indicators of Hyperinflation
question: Which of the following economic conditions is a key characteristic of a hyperinflationary economy under Ind AS 29?
options: Annual GDP growth exceeds 10%.

The cumulative inflation rate over a three-year period is approaching, or exceeds, 100%, and the general population prefers to keep its wealth in non-monetary assets or in a relatively stable foreign currency.
The central bank increases interest rates by 25 basis points.
Stock market valuations decline for two consecutive quarters.
ref: Ind AS 29 (Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies) - Paragraph 3: Indicators of Hyperinflation
explanation: Ind AS 29 Paragraph 3 lists characteristics of hyperinflation: (a) general population prefers wealth in non-monetary assets or stable foreign currency; (b) prices quoted in foreign currency; (c) credit sales compensate for expected loss of purchasing power; (d) interest rates and wages linked to a price index; and (e) the cumulative inflation rate over three years is approaching, or exceeds, 100%.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 29: Restatement of Financial Statements
question: Under Ind AS 29, when an entity's functional currency is the currency of a hyperinflationary economy, how are its financial statements stated?
options: Stated in terms of the measuring unit current at the end of the reporting period by applying a General Price Index to non-monetary items, with the gain or loss on the net monetary position recognized in Profit or Loss.
Translated into USD at the historical exchange rate of 10 years ago.
Prepared strictly on a cash basis.
Non-monetary items are frozen at book value.
ref: Ind AS 29 - Paragraphs 8-9: Restatement in Constant Currency
explanation: Under Ind AS 29, the financial statements of an entity whose functional currency is hyperinflationary are stated in terms of the measuring unit current at the end of the reporting period. Balance sheet non-monetary items not already expressed in current measuring units are restated using a general price index. The gain or loss on the net monetary position is recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Advance Payments for Non-Monetary Assets (Appendix B / IFRIC 22)
question: On 1st February 2024, Indian Importer Ltd. pays a non-refundable advance of $100,000 (exchange rate $1 = ₹82) to a US machine vendor for customized equipment. On 31st March 2024, the exchange rate is $1 = ₹84. On 15th April 2024 (when $1 = ₹85), the machinery is delivered. Under Appendix B of Ind AS 21, what is the initial cost of the machinery capitalized on 15th April 2024?
options: ₹82,00,000 ($100,000 × advance payment transaction date rate ₹82), because the date of the transaction for the purpose of determining the exchange rate on initial recognition of the non-monetary asset is the date on which the entity initially recognized the non-monetary advance asset.
Average rate of ₹83.50.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Appendix B (Foreign Currency Transactions and Advance Consideration)
explanation: Appendix B Paragraph 8 states that the date of the transaction for the purpose of determining the exchange rate to use on initial recognition of the related asset, expense, or income is the date on which an entity initially recognizes the non-monetary asset or non-monetary liability arising from the payment or receipt of advance consideration. Because the advance was paid on 1st February at ₹82, that historical rate applies to the machinery.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Exchange Differences on Borrowing Costs
question: An entity borrows USD 10,000,000 on 1st April 2023 at 5% interest per annum to construct a qualifying manufacturing plant. Local INR borrowings would have carried interest at 10% per annum. During the year, the exchange rate moved from $1 = ₹80 to $1 = ₹83 (exchange loss ₹3 Crores). How much of the ₹3 Crores exchange loss can be capitalized under Ind AS 23 and Ind AS 21 as an adjustment to borrowing costs?
options: The entire ₹3 Crores exchange loss is capitalized.

The exchange difference is capitalized only to the extent that it represents an adjustment to interest costs (the difference between local borrowing costs of 10% on ₹80 Cr = ₹8 Cr, and foreign borrowing costs of 5% on ₹80 Cr = ₹4 Cr, meaning up to ₹4 Crores of exchange difference can be treated as borrowing cost); here, the full ₹3 Crores exchange loss is capitalized as borrowing cost.
Zero; all exchange differences are expensed to P&L under Ind AS 21.
Recognized in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 6(e) & Ind AS 21: Exchange Differences as Borrowing Costs
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 6(e) states that borrowing costs include exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings to the extent that they are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs. The equivalent local borrowing cost is ₹80 Cr × 10% = ₹8 Cr. Foreign interest paid = $500,000 × ₹83 (approx ₹4.15 Cr). Since foreign interest + ₹3 Cr exchange loss = ₹7.15 Cr < ₹8 Cr, the entire ₹3 Cr exchange loss is treated as an adjustment to borrowing costs.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Change in Functional Currency
question: Due to a fundamental shift in business model, Star India Ltd.'s functional currency changed from INR to USD on 1st October 2023. Under Ind AS 21, how is a change in functional currency accounted for?
options: Retrospectively, restating all prior years as if USD had always been the functional currency.

Prospectively from the date of the change: the entity translates all items into the new functional currency using the exchange rate at the date of the change; the resulting translated amounts for non-monetary items are treated as their historical cost.
The change is prohibited under Indian Company Law.
Recognized directly in Retained Earnings.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraphs 35-37: Accounting for a Change in Functional Currency
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 35 states that when there is a change in an entity's functional currency, the entity shall apply the translation procedures applicable to the new functional currency prospectively from the date of the change. All items are translated into the new functional currency at the spot rate on the date of change, and non-monetary items are treated as their new historical cost.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Foreign Currency Dividend Received from Subsidiary
question: Indian Parent receives a cash dividend of USD 1,000,000 from its US subsidiary. At the date of dividend receipt, the exchange rate is $1 = ₹83. In Parent Ltd.'s standalone financial statements, at what amount is dividend income recognized?
options: ₹8,30,00,000 (USD 1,000,000 translated at the spot exchange rate on the date of receipt/entitlement).
Historical exchange rate at which the initial share capital was invested.
Average exchange rate of the financial year.
Zero, because intra-group dividends are eliminated in standalone accounts.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 21: Initial Recognition of Foreign Currency Transactions
explanation: A foreign currency transaction shall be recorded, on initial recognition in the functional currency, by applying to the foreign currency amount the spot exchange rate between the functional currency and the foreign currency at the date of the transaction. The dividend is recognized at $1M × ₹83 = ₹8.3 Crores.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Goodwill of a Foreign Operation
question: Indian Parent Ltd. acquired a French subsidiary whose functional currency is the Euro (EUR). In the purchase price allocation, goodwill of €10,000,000 arose on acquisition. Under Ind AS 21, how is this goodwill treated at each subsequent balance sheet date?
options: Treated as an asset of the Indian Parent and fixed permanently at the historical acquisition INR rate.

Treated as an asset of the foreign operation (Euro-denominated asset); it is expressed in the functional currency of the foreign operation and translated at the closing exchange rate at each reporting date, with exchange differences recognized in OCI (FCTR).
Amortized over 5 years.
Expensed in full in P&L.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 47: Goodwill Arising on Acquisition of a Foreign Operation
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 47 states explicitly: 'Any goodwill arising on the acquisition of a foreign operation and any fair value adjustments to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities arising on the acquisition of that foreign operation shall be treated as assets and liabilities of the foreign operation. Thus, they shall be expressed in the functional currency of the foreign operation and shall be translated at the closing rate.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Long-Term Foreign Currency Monetary Item Exemption (FCMITDA)
question: Under Companies (Ind AS) Rules, Paragraph 46A of Ind AS 21 provides a transitional relief for long-term foreign currency monetary items recognized before 1st April 2016. Which option did it grant?
options: Mandatory hedging of all foreign debt.

The option to accumulate exchange differences relating to long-term foreign currency monetary items in a 'Foreign Currency Monetary Item Translation Difference Account' (FCMITDA) and amortize it over the life of the monetary item, or add/deduct it from the cost of depreciable capital assets.
Complete exemption from financial reporting.
Option to revalue monetary assets.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 46A: Transitional Relief on Long-Term Foreign Currency Monetary Items
explanation: Paragraph 46A was inserted into Ind AS 21 in India to provide continuity for companies that had elected the option under AS 11 (Paragraph 46/46A). It permitted capitalizing foreign exchange differences on long-term foreign currency borrowings into the cost of depreciable assets or accumulating them in FCMITDA.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 29: Monetary Loss Calculation
question: At the start of the year, an enterprise in a hyperinflationary economy holds cash and trade receivables of 1,00,000 local currency units (LCU) and bank debt of 40,000 LCU (net monetary asset = 60,000 LCU). The general price index doubles (100% inflation) during the year. What is the impact on the net monetary position?
options: A purchasing power gain of 60,000 LCU.
A net purchasing power loss on monetary assets of 60,000 LCU recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss, because holding monetary assets during inflation results in a loss of purchasing power.
No gain or loss arises on monetary items.
Recognized in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 29 - Paragraph 9 & Paragraph 28: Gain or Loss on Net Monetary Position
explanation: In a period of inflation, an entity holding an excess of monetary assets over monetary liabilities loses purchasing power, and an entity with an excess of monetary liabilities over monetary assets gains purchasing power to the extent the obligations are not linked to a price level. The resulting gain or loss on the net monetary position is recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Foreign Currency Borrowings Fair Value Adjustment
question: An entity issues bonds denominated in Euro. The bond carries a fixed interest rate. When translating the foreign currency bond at the balance sheet date under Ind AS 21 (carried at amortized cost), how are the changes in exchange rate recognized?
options: In Other Comprehensive Income.
In the Statement of Profit and Loss as foreign exchange fluctuation gain or loss.
Deferred as a discount on bonds.
Adjusted against equity share capital.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 28: Recognition of Exchange Differences on Monetary Items
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 28 specifies that exchange differences arising on the settlement of monetary items or on translating monetary items at rates different from those at which they were translated on initial recognition or in previous financial statements shall be recognized in profit or loss in the period in which they arise.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Presentation Currency Choice
question: An Indian corporate entity has INR as its functional currency. The Board of Directors wishes to present its consolidated financial statements in US Dollars (USD) to attract international institutional investors. Is this permissible under Ind AS 21?
options: No, Indian entities must always present their financial statements in Indian Rupees by law.

Yes, Ind AS 21 Paragraph 38 states that an entity may present its financial statements in any currency (or currencies); if the presentation currency differs from the functional currency, the entity translates its results and financial position into the presentation currency using standard translation procedures.
Permissible only if approved by the Reserve Bank of India.
Permissible only if turnover exceeds ₹10,000 Crores.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 38: Choice of Presentation Currency
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 38 explicitly states: 'An entity may present its financial statements in any currency (or currencies).' If the presentation currency differs from the entity's functional currency, its results and financial position are translated into the presentation currency in accordance with paragraphs 39-43.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Partial Disposal of Subsidiary with FCTR Allocation
question: Parent Ltd. sells a 20% stake in its wholly-owned foreign subsidiary for ₹30 Crores, reducing its ownership from 100% to 80% without losing control. Cumulative FCTR relating to the subsidiary is ₹10 Crores. How is FCTR treated on this partial disposal?
options: ₹2 Crores (20% of FCTR) is recycled to Profit or Loss.

No FCTR is reclassified to Profit or Loss; instead, the proportionate share of cumulative exchange differences (20% of ₹10 Cr = ₹2 Crores) is reattributed to the Non-Controlling Interest (NCI) within equity.
The entire ₹10 Crores FCTR is recycled to P&L.
FCTR is transferred to Capital Reserve.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 48A: Partial Disposal of a Subsidiary Without Loss of Control
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 48A specifies: 'On the partial disposal of a subsidiary that includes a foreign operation, the entity shall re-attribute the proportionate share of the cumulative amount of the exchange differences recognized in other comprehensive income to the non-controlling interests in that foreign operation.' It is an equity transaction; no recycling to P&L occurs.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 21: Cumulative Translation Differences in Inter-Company Eliminations
question: Parent Ltd. sells goods to foreign subsidiary Sub Ltd. Sub Ltd. owes Parent Ltd. $5,000,000. In Parent's books (INR functional), an exchange gain of ₹2 Crores arises on this monetary balance. When preparing consolidated financial statements, how is this exchange gain treated?
options: The exchange gain is eliminated in full against consolidated profit.

Because the monetary item represents a commitment to convert one currency into another, it exposes the group to a currency fluctuation risk; therefore, in consolidated financial statements, the exchange difference is NOT eliminated, but continues to be recognized in consolidated Profit or Loss (unless it forms part of a net investment under Paragraph 15).
Recognized in OCI.
Transferred to NCI.
ref: Ind AS 21 - Paragraph 45: Intra-Group Foreign Exchange Differences in Consolidation
explanation: Ind AS 21 Paragraph 45 explains that an intra-group monetary asset or liability cannot be eliminated without showing the results of currency fluctuations in the consolidated financial statements. This is because the monetary item represents a commitment to convert one currency into another and exposes the group to a currency risk. Accordingly, such an exchange difference continues to be recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 29: Economy Ceasing to be Hyperinflationary
question: When an economy ceases to be hyperinflationary and an entity discontinues the preparation of financial statements in accordance with Ind AS 29, what is the accounting treatment for carrying amounts?
options: All assets must be restated back to original historical costs before hyperinflation.
The entity shall treat the amounts expressed in the measuring unit current at the end of the previous reporting period as the basis for the carrying amounts in its subsequent financial statements.
All reserves must be capitalized into equity shares.
The entity must liquidate its operating divisions.
ref: Ind AS 29 - Paragraph 38: Cessation of Hyperinflation
explanation: Ind AS 29 Paragraph 38 states: 'When an economy ceases to be hyperinflationary and an entity discontinues the preparation and presentation of financial statements in accordance with this Standard, it shall treat the amounts expressed in the measuring unit current at the end of the previous reporting period as the basis for the carrying amounts in its subsequent financial statements.'
